entities.name: Alfonso I d'Este
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Alfonso I d'Este was a pivotal figure in the Italian Wars, serving as Duke of Ferrara, Modena, and Reggio from 1505 until his death in 1534. A skilled military leader, he earned the nickname Duca Artigliere for his innovative use of artillery.

As a prominent leader during this period, Alfonso I d'Este played a significant role in shaping the fate of Italy. He collaborated with various factions, including the French and Spanish armies, to further his own interests.

Alfonso's legacy extends beyond his military exploits, as he also contributed to the development of Ferrara as a major cultural center. His innovative approach to artillery had a lasting impact on warfare tactics, influencing future generations of military leaders.

Despite his significant contributions to Italian history, Alfonso I d'Este remains somewhat overshadowed by more prominent figures of the time. However, his enduring legacy serves as a testament to the enduring power of human ingenuity and strategic thinking.
